SMTO-HTTP-0062 — SMTO couldn't reuse a remembered connection setup

GUID: af33027d-9ba8-4e32-b93d-b69dd141ec44
Slug: http-saved-context-invalid
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO remembers how it connected to a service so later steps can reuse it. That remembered setup didn't check out, so SMTO set it aside and needs to connect again. Your saved connection in Parameter Store wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reply in the Conversation asking the Agent to connect to the service again using its saved connection. A new connection replaces the remembered setup that SMTO set aside.
  2. If connecting fails, open the connection in Parameter Store and select Test connection to see whether the saved settings still work. The test shows whether the problem is in the saved connection itself rather than the remembered setup.
  3. If the test reports a problem, choose Reveal & edit value, correct the Base URL or Authentication settings, select Save, and ask the Agent to connect again. SMTO can only remember a setup it can rebuild exactly from a valid saved connection.

What success looks like

  • The Agent connects to the service and its later web requests work without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the saved connection; it isn't damaged, only the remembered copy was set aside.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An HTTP Working Context setup failed validation (field set, profile key, 64-hex profile digest, canonical compact public profile, Gateway identity or transport, or the connection-auth compiler round-trip), so it was not carried forward for reuse.

What this means

  • HTTP working setup fails its closed schema, digest, canonical public-profile, Gateway route identity or compiled authentication-recipe consistency check. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • HTTP working setup fails its closed schema, digest, canonical public-profile, Gateway route identity or compiled authentication-recipe consistency check.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare its exact fields, canonical profile digest and Gateway transport identity with a fresh accepted connection.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the conversation's Working Context entry for this HTTP resource and its source run. Reconnect with http.connect using the saved profile (or a valid one-off recipe) so a fresh verified setup is published. If the profile's auth cannot round-trip through compile_connection_auth, fix that auth configuration in Parameter Store.
  • Reopen the intended connection profile, reconnect through its verified route, and rebuild working context from the current connection.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Working setup is rebuilt from a valid current connection with matching canonical values.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
